summary: Farmers worldwide face escalating climate pressures, including shifting temperatures, erratic rainfall, water scarcity, and declining soil health. Selecting the right crop rotation to protect fields and conserve water has become increasingly complex. RAWD is a web-based decision-support tool that bridges the gap between space data and local agriculture. By integrating live NASA Earth observations—specifically NASA POWER agroclimatology metrics alongside SMAP soil moisture and GPM precipitation indicators—with local soil types and farmer priorities, RAWD generates tailored, 3-season crop rotation strategies. Our tool empowers farmers to optimize water usage, restore soil nitrogen naturally, and build long-term climate resilience through actionable, easy-to-understand planting schedules.
details:
What it does & How it works:

RAWD is an accessible web-based decision-support tool designed for farmers. It takes simple user inputs (farm coordinates, local soil type, and farmer priorities) and connects directly to live NASA Earth observations (NASA POWER API) to analyze local climate, soil moisture, and precipitation stress. It then outputs a customized 3-season crop rotation strategy.

Benefits & Impact:

It helps farmers conserve water, restore soil health naturally without synthetic fertilizers, and adapt their fields to climate change and extreme weather.

Tools & Technologies Used:

HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (Fetch API), GitHub for version control, and NASA POWER Agroclimatology API.

Creativity & Factors Considered:

RAWD bridges complex satellite remote sensing data with hyper-local, practical agricultural needs, providing an intuitive interface tailored for smallholder farmers.
